subject: Dedicated sizing proposal & latency-bucket throughput model for Acrophio
body:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@acrophio.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acrophio.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing for initial commit and latency targets

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the quick chat today. Acrophio is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a staged launch: 2 phases (pilot -> GA). Primary constraints: conversational chat (turns up to 1k tokens), bursty peak usage for new users, and strict p95 generation latency <= 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens).

Can you share a sizing proposal that maps our expected token/sec during peak, recommended GPU slabs (quantized vs fp16 tradeoffs), and minimal headroom to keep p95 within the SLO if we commit to a 2M token/month slab initially?

Also attaching our traffic shape (hourly) and a short mutual action checklist.

Best,
Elena Park
Ops Lead, Acrophio
[Attachment: acrophio_traffic_shape.csv]

----
On Tue, 25 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700 wrote:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acrophio.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for initial commit and latency targets

Elena — thanks for the details and the traffic file. I did a quick pass and put together a throughput/latency-bucket model attached. High-level summary below; spreadsheet is the source of the numbers.

Key assumptions:
- Model family: MPT-30B-Chat (open fine-tuned baseline) at two execution profiles: INT8-quantized (1) and FP16 (2).
- Typical prompt/response mix: 70% short (<128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long (>512).
- Warm cache for 60% of requests during peak (prefix KV cache hit rate).
- Target p95 SLO: 350ms for short prompts, 550ms for medium.

Estimated tokens/sec (peak 15-min rolling window):
- Short bucket (<=128 tokens): 18k tokens/sec (after our conversion from requests/sec and avg tokens)
- Medium bucket (129-512 tokens): 6k tokens/sec
- Long bucket (>512 tokens): 800 tokens/sec
- Aggregate peak tokens/sec: ~24.8k tps

GPU mapping recommendation (initial 2M token/month commitment):
- If using INT8 quantized kernels: recommended slab = 8x A100-80GB equivalent (quantized throughput scheduling), expected sustained aggregate capacity ~28k tps with target latency bands met and ~12% headroom.
- If using FP16 execution: recommended slab = 12x A100-80GB equivalent to hit same latency bands; higher infra cost but simpler QA baseline.

Headroom analysis and graceful degradation:
- With the INT8 slab above we expect p95 short <= 320ms with 12% headroom. If 15%+ unexpected burst occurs (e.g., marketing campaign), fallback plan: route non-critical medium/long requests to a lower-cost variant (smaller-context model) and throttle conversational features for anonymous users.
- Cold-start scenarios (cache miss heavy) add ~60–85ms to short p95; we account for that in the attached latency_tail_bucket_analysis.pdf.

Action requested: can we confirm preferred execution profile (INT8 vs FP16) and whether Acrophio wants us to reserve burst tokens for the launch week (recommended)? I added a proposed mutual action plan in the XL and a doc link at the bottom.

Thanks — I can walk through the sheet tomorrow.

— Karthik Iy er
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acrophio_commit_capacity_model.xlsx]

----
On Wed, 26 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700 wrote:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Elena Park <elena.park@acrophio.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for initial commit and latency targets

Looping in a quick ops/quantization note.

We recommend the INT8 path for cost/perf — but two engineering notes: 1) quantized kernels are more sensitive to peak concurrency shapes; if Acrophio plans to enable multi-turn assistants with heavy context windows, we'd need to reduce concurrency caps per-GPU or add an extra 1–2 GPU equivalents as buffer (we modeled this as a "concurrency cushion" in the sheet). 2) If Acrophio expects a marketing-driven burst (50%+ traffic spike for a day), enable the Reserved Burst option in the Dedicated contract for predictable capacity — otherwise our autoscaler can add cloud burst but will not meet the p95 SLO during a cold resize.

Operational asks we put in the MAP:
- Sign the MOU for initial 2M tokens/month commit by EOD next week.
- Approve INT8 execution for GA (pilot can be FP16).
- Confirm whether they want a reserved 24‑hour burst for launch (we recommend yes).

I'll attach a short runbook excerpt for cache warm-up to reduce cold-start tail; it's a 1-page checklist.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency_tail_bucket_analysis.pdf]

----
On Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700 wrote:
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena.park@acrophio.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for initial commit and latency targets

Elena — quick commercial note. Based on the INT8 slab recommendation and the requested reserved burst option, we can structure the initial Dedicated commitment as: 2M tokens/month base commit (12-month term) + one 24-hour launch burst reserve (priced as 48 hours of spare capacity pro-rated). That gets you the 12% headroom Karthik modeled and guaranteed p95 for the launch window.

If you want to proceed, I'll generate the MOU and add the reserved-burst clause to the SLA addendum. If Acrophio needs a lower cap on unit price, we can move to a 24-month term and revisit pricing.

Next step: Elena, can you confirm by end-of-day Monday whether we should draft the MOU with the reserved-burst clause? I'll attach the MAP we discussed.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: acrophio_mutual_action_plan.md]
